equity_bridge.item: Residual cash restructuring (Le Havre F4 closure, Saverglass corporate restructure, RAK idling)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 cash significant items were A$50.5m and are excluded from underlying EBITDA. A further ~A$30m is assumed to be paid in FY2027 against provisions already raised; analyst estimate, not disclosed.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: analyst judgment from FY2026 continuing-operations segment trends; reported CAGRs rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported CAGRs are not usable. Revenue falls because OPS (about A$3bn of revenue) was sold in December 2024; equity rises because of the FY2024 entitlement offer and the FY2025 disposal gain, then falls on the FY2026 impairment; statutory EPS is negative in FY2026. Equity CAGR diverges from revenue CAGR by far more than 30 points. The only like-for-like data point is continuing revenue FY2025 to FY2026: +6.5% reported, +5.7% constant currency (Cans +13.3% including aluminium pass-through, Glass +2.5%).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2021 212.6, FY2023 55.2, FY2026 75.9. SBC is under 0.3% of revenue throughout, so owner and reported FCF growth are effectively the same. Underlying EPS before significant items was flat at 11.4 cents in FY2025 and FY2026.

scenario_narratives.base: Cans keeps growing volume at the low end of management's 4-6% long-term range on capacity that is now built (Rocklea commissions in Q1 FY27 and no new capacity is needed until after 2030), so growth capex falls away and Cans earnings grow with operating leverage. Glass stays dull: Saverglass volumes hold but mix and price stay weak for another year or two as the premium spirits and wine downturn drags on, RAK runs on restricted volume, and Gawler slowly loses beer volume against contracted price rises. Management delivers about half of its target of more than EUR30m of Glass EBIT run-rate improvement by FY30. Group EBITDA margin dips to 18.5% in FY27 then recovers to about 20%, the FY2025 level, and capex settles near depreciation.
scenario_narratives.bull: The spirits destocking cycle ends and premium mix recovers, so Saverglass regains price and its EBIT margin moves back toward the 12.9% of FY2025 and beyond; the Le Havre closure and Ghlin modernisation lift utilisation and the full EUR30m-plus improvement is delivered. Cans grows at 6% with a richer format mix (energy, soft drinks, the new 375ml line) and converts it at high incremental margins. Group EBITDA margin reaches 22% and revenue grows 4-5% for five years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The premium spirits and wine decline is structural rather than cyclical (moderation, tariffs, cost of living), so Saverglass keeps trading volume for price, more furnaces are idled, and the Middle East disruption to RAK persists; the FY2026 impairment proves to be the first of two. Gawler beer volumes keep falling. Cans growth slows to 2-3% and major customer contracts reprice at renewal. Group EBITDA margin drifts to 17%, furnace rebuilds keep capex at 6.5% or more of revenue, and revenue is flat in FY27 and grows below inflation after.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Orora is valued on the continuing two-business portfolio (Cans and Glass) using FY2026 underlying earnings before significant items as the base, with the non-cash impairment and the disposal gains of earlier years excluded. Free cash flow is built from components so that the end of the Cans growth-capex cycle shows up as lower capex, while maintenance capex is held near depreciation because glass furnaces must be rebuilt. The terminal value is capped at 14 times free cash flow, which binds in the base and bull cases, reflecting a capital-intensive packaging business and not a compounder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Saverglass: a further fall in premium spirits and wine demand or price would cut Glass margin and could trigger a second impairment and more furnace closures
Maintenance capex: if furnace rebuild needs run above the 6.2% of revenue assumed, value falls roughly in proportion to the shortfall in free cash flow
Cans customer concentration and contract renewals in a two-supplier Australian market

Cash restructuring costs are booked as significant items outside underlying EBITDA; only A$30m of future cash cost is deducted, and repeat charges would mean underlying margins overstate cash earnings
EUR/AUD translation: about half of revenue is Saverglass, reported in euros
No post-result trading update was reviewed; the year-1 margin is an estimate, not guidance

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.212-2.43
data_sources.financials: Orora FY2026 Annual Report (group financial review, segment note 1.1, cash flow statement, EPS note, net debt note) and ORA.AX_Metrics.csv; FY2025 Annual Report for comparatives
data_sources.qualitative: FY2026 Annual Report chair and CEO letters and operational reviews; ORA.AX_Analysis.json was not yet available

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,225.343m shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR five-year summary) plus 10.9m potential ordinary shares from employee options and rights (FY2026 AR EPS note). Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows. The weighted-average diluted figure (1,255.5m) is NOT used because it predates most of the FY2026 buyback.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement, share-based payment expense A$3.5m (note 6.1). No separate equity-award tax line; awards are settled with treasury shares bought on market (A$3.1m in FY2026).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:11:16Z regular ASX close (Friday; valuation run on a weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5%, built in AUD: risk-free ~4.4% (AU 10-year), equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~0.95 gives cost of equity ~9.6%; after-tax cost of debt ~4%; ~20% debt weight. Roughly half the flows are EUR (Saverglass) where the risk-free rate is lower, so 8.5% leans conservative. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: glass-market risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost). Lease cash cost charged inside the flows at 1.6% of revenue (FY2026: A$29.1m principal in financing plus lease interest; the segment note shows A$29.7m of right-of-use lease payments, rounded up for interest). Lease liabilities of A$181.8m are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use amortisation (FY2026: 172.1 total less 25.2 ROU = 146.9, 6.6% of revenue).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, single lease treatment, near-zero SBC). Chosen because Orora is an operating manufacturer (beverage cans in Australia/NZ, premium glass via Saverglass plus Gawler); no prior valuation or memory entry exists. BASIS: the forward build starts from FY2026 CONTINUING operations (Cans A$880.0m + Glass A$1,345.9m revenue; underlying EBITDA A$420.3m, 18.9%; underlying EBIT A$248.2m; underlying NPAT A$142.2m). History before FY2025 is not comparable: Fibre sold FY2020 with a 4-for-5 consolidation, Saverglass bought Dec 2023 with an entitlement offer, OPS sold Dec 2024. FY2020 and FY2025 net income carry disposal gains and FY2026 carries a A$742.8m non-cash Glass impairment (A$782.2m total significant items pre-tax); none of the three is used as an earnings base. last_fcf (75.9 = reported 79.4 less SBC 3.5) is a LEVERED figure after A$59.2m interest paid, A$108.4m growth capex and A$50.5m cash significant items, and before A$29.1m lease principal; it is recorded for the contract and is not what the projection compounds from. Interest income (A$4.6m) is not stripped because the company is in net debt. BUYBACK: A$117.6m spent in FY2026 (56.0m shares); the second programme was paused on 9 April 2026, so the flat count is a convention, not a funded commitment. NET DEBT: borrowings 978.1 less cash 513.1 = 465.0 per the FY2026 net debt note; A$284.1m of revolver was repaid from cash in July 2026, which shrinks both sides and leaves net debt unchanged. NOT CHECKED: no AGM or trading update after the August 2026 result was available in the research folder; the price is well below its 52-week high, so a post-result downgrade may exist and would move year-1 margin. Analysis JSON was not yet written when this was built; scenario axes come from the FY2026 Annual Report.

base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex was A$194.3m (8.7%): base A$85.9m plus growth A$108.4m. Year 1 keeps 8.0% for the Rocklea third line (commissioning Q1 FY27) and the Ghlin furnace rebuild. Thereafter 6.2%, deliberately above FY2026 base capex of 3.9%, because glass furnaces need periodic rebuilds and base capex well below depreciation (6.6%) is not sustainable. The terminal year is set equal to D&A.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 underlying EBITDA margin 18.9% (FY2025 20.0%). Year 1 dips to 18.5% for the second-half Glass weakness and RAK running on restricted volume. The climb to 20.2% credits Cans operating leverage on the completed capacity programme and roughly half of management's target of more than EUR30m Glass EBIT run-rate improvement by FY30.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 underlying tax expense A$49.4m on A$191.6m pre-tax profit is 25.8%. Cash tax paid was only A$27.0m; the model does not carry that shortfall forward.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% default: the A$742.8m impairment is management's own admission that Saverglass is earning well below the acquisition case, conditions worsened in the second half of FY2026, and Glass is 60% of revenue; it is not higher because leverage is 1.2x EBITDA with no core refinancing until FY30, so the downside is margin erosion and not solvency. Base 50%: Cans delivery plus partial Glass self-help. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs a spirits-market recovery outside management's control and full delivery of the Glass improvement programme at the same time.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
